🌲🇲🇽 PROFEPA SHUTS DOWN ILLEGAL MINE AFTER INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES SPOKE UP

Federal environmental inspectors, backed by the Navy and state forest police, ordered the total closure of an illegal feldspar mine in Zacatlán, Puebla — operating with no environmental-impact permit and clearing protected Sierra Norte forest. The trigger: formal complaints from local Indigenous residents. Authorities are now reviewing all nine active mining concessions in the municipality.

🔥🇲🇽 "WE NEVER MAKE DEALS WITH CARTELS — WHO DOES?" SHEINBAUM FLIPS THE SCRIPT

Sheinbaum: "Mexico's government makes no agreements with cartel members... who negotiates with organized crime? We don't; we never will." She pointed the question back at US agencies — which granted Ovidio Guzmán benefits on July 25, 2024 — and at the PAN's Genaro García Luna, convicted in New York of taking Sinaloa Cartel money.

🚨🇲🇽 HOMICIDES IN SINALOA DOWN 44% UNDER THE 4T SECURITY STRATEGY

Daily intentional homicides in Sinaloa fell 44% from June 2025 to July 2026, alongside 2,540 arrests and over 94.5 tons of drugs seized. Security chief Omar García Harfuch said the strategy "targets all criminal structures generating violence," not a single faction — results built by Mexican forces, without a militarized US "assistance" mission.

🇲🇽🌎 EUROPE OPENS UP — PARLIAMENT RATIFIES MODERNIZED MEXICO-EU GLOBAL AGREEMENT

The European Parliament ratified the modernized EU-Mexico Global Agreement on July 8 with 479 votes in favor, eliminating tariffs on 99% of goods traded. Ebrard expects a boost for Mexican agricultural exports. While Washington threatens annual T-MEC reviews, Mexico keeps widening its markets — trade doesn't have to run only north.

🚨🇲🇽 MEXICO GOES BEYOND DIPLOMATIC NOTES AFTER ICE KILLS ANOTHER MEXICAN

An ICE agent shot and killed Lorenzo Salgado Araujo during a July 7 operation in Houston — at least the 16th Mexican to die in ICE custody or operations since Trump returned. Sheinbaum said Mexico will act "más allá de notas diplomáticas," filing legal resources in US courts and international bodies: "we cannot allow the mistreatment of our brothers who are in the United States."

REUTERS: Latin American countries, some steelmakers argue for US tariff exemptions
July 7, 2026

The Trump administration wants 10–12.5% tariffs on 59 countries — Mexico among them — to "punish" lax enforcement of forced-labor laws. Mexico, Peru, Guatemala and Ecuador rejected the premise at the USTR hearing. The tell: US steelmakers lined up for the very same exemption, because they can't make steel without the imported pig iron the tariff would tax.

A "forced labor" pretext aimed at suppliers Washington's own mills depend on.

• ministers "rejected allegations they are failing to enforce laws against forced labor"
• without exemptions, pig iron could hit "37.5%," US producers at "a competitive disadvantage"

WASHINGTON POST: English fans thought they were soccer-mad. Then they went to Mexico.
July 6, 2026

After weeks of US coverage warning of hotel sieges, fireworks and danger around the Mexico–England match, the Post sent reporters to the Azteca and found England fans calling Mexico City "a soccer lover's paradise inhabited by kindred spirits." Credit where it's due — a fair one.

The same fans who'd seen the viral "menace" clips said nothing in Qatar or three European Championships compared with the welcome they got in Mexico.

• "a soccer lover's paradise inhabited by kindred spirits"
• "nothing they had experienced compared with what they found in Mexico City"

CBS NEWS: Mexico investigating possible U.S. violation in 2024 capture of "El Mayo"
July 7, 2026

Mexico opened a sovereignty probe after the FBI put the plane used to fly "El Mayo" Zambada out of the country on public display. The US Embassy swore in 2024 that "no U.S. agency participated." Then Guzman Lopez pleaded guilty to kidnapping Zambada across the border.

US headlines say "Mexico questions" the FBI — but it was Washington's own exhibit and its own defendant's plea that exposed the denial.

• "The versions are contradictory. Someone lied." — Rosa Icela Rodriguez
• "Everything seems to indicate that the ambassador lied." — Sheinbaum

🇲🇽🏭 DESPITE TARIFFS, MEXICO SETS AN EXPORT RECORD AND IS NOW THE US'S #1 SUPPLIER

Mexico shipped $54.18 billion to the United States in May — the highest single month ever recorded, up 17.5% year-on-year (US Census Bureau). It now accounts for 17.4% of all US imports, ahead of Canada (11.7%), China (7.5%) and Germany (4.3%), with $558 billion in sales over the last 12 months. The tariffs meant to punish Mexico left it as America's single largest trading partner.

🔥🇲🇽 MEXICO BARS TWO FIRMS FROM FEDERAL CONTRACTS FOR FAKING BIDS

The Secretariat of Anti-Corruption and Good Governance sanctioned two companies for lying in federal tenders. Impulsora Cordobesa faked three contracts to inflate its experience while bidding to supply food to IMSS clinics — a 643,188-peso fine and a one-year ban; a second firm was barred three months for a bad-faith bid on motorcycle helmets. Both now sit in the public Directory of Sanctioned Providers.
